The '''Varunastra''' ({{Lit|[[Astra (weapon)]] of [[Varuna]]}}) is an Indian advanced autonomous heavyweight [[anti-submarine]] [[torpedo]], developed by the [[Naval Science and Technological Laboratory]] (NSTL) of the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO) for the [[Indian Navy]]. It is named after a [[Varunastra|legendary weapon]] created by the [[Hindu deities|Hindu god]] of the oceans, ''[[Varuna]]''.<ref name="Siddiqui">{{Cite web |last=Siddiqui |first=Huma |date=2023-06-07 |title=Varunastra Torpedo to enhance Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, Know all about its powerful features here |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/defence-varunastra-torpedo-to-enhance-indian-navys-anti-submarine-warfare-capabilities-know-all-about-its-powerful-features-here-3117020/ |access-date=2023-12-29 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref>

== Design ==
This torpedo is powered by an electric propulsion system with multiple {{convert|250|kW||abbr=on}} [[Silver oxide battery|Silver Oxide]]-Zinc (AgOZn) batteries.<ref name="varunastraIndiaStrategic">{{cite web |url=http://www.indiastrategic.in/topstories3130_Indian_navy_ships_rely_on_DRDO_technology.htm |title=Indian Navy's most powerful ships rely on DRDO technology |website=indiastrategic.in |access-date=30 June 2016 |archive-date=16 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160716205939/http://indiastrategic.in/topstories3130_Indian_navy_ships_rely_on_DRDO_technology.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> It can achieve speeds in excess of {{convert|40|kn|abbr=on}}, weighs around 1.5 tonnes and can carry {{convert|250|kg|lb|abbr=on}} of conventional warhead. This torpedo has more than 95 per cent indigenous content. Varunastra has conformal array [[transducer]] which enables it look at wider angles than most common torpedoes. It also has an advanced autonomous guidance algorithms with low drift navigational aids, insensitive warhead which can operate in various combat scenarios. It is the only torpedo in the world to have a GPS-based locating aid.<ref name="varunastraRediff" /><ref name="varunastraFinancialExp">{{cite web |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/india-news/varunastra-5-things-to-know-about-the-lethal-drdo-torpedo-for-indian-navy/301924/ |title=Varunastra: 5 things to know about the lethal DRDO torpedo for Indian Navy |date=30 June 2016 |access-date=6 July 2016 |work=The Financial Express |first=Smriti |last=Jain}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-06-07 |title=Varunastra Torpedo to enhance Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, Know all about its powerful features here |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/defence-varunastra-torpedo-to-enhance-indian-navys-anti-submarine-warfare-capabilities-know-all-about-its-powerful-features-here-3117020/#google_vignette |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}}</ref> The exercise variant of Varunastra has integrated instrumentation system for recording all the dynamic parameters of the weapon, redundancy in recovery aids in case of emergency shut down or malfunction.<ref name="varunastraRediff" />

== Development ==
In May 2014 it was reported that the [[Indian Navy]] is scheduled to carry out User Evaluation Trials (UETs) during the mid-year period. The assembly of the prototype was done by a team from [[Bharat Dynamics Limited]] at the Talwar facility of NSTL in [[Visakhapatnam]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2014-02-28 |title=Varunastra to undergo evaluation trials soon |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/varunastra-to-undergo-evaluation-trials-soon/article5737344.ece |access-date=2024-10-15 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

In the [[Fiscal year|financial year]] 2015-16, the torpedo underwent 130 technical trials while 14 user trials were conducted between January and March 2015. In September 2015, MoD granted final approval for the torpedo's User Evaluation Trials (UETs) and eventually it was accepted for induction into Services.<ref name=":1" />

The development of the first variant — ship-launched, anti-submarine variant — of the torpedo was completed in July 2016. The overall development period was 11 years.<ref name="varunastraIndianExp" />

The variant of Varunastra torpedo was formally inducted in the Indian Navy by defence minister [[Manohar Parrikar]] on 26 June 2016.<ref name="varunastraNewsX" /><ref name="varunastraIndianExp">{{cite web|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/india/india-news-india/anti-submarine-torpedo-varunastra-inducted-in-navy/|title=Anti-submarine torpedo Varunastra inducted in Navy|work=The Indian Express|date=29 June 2016|access-date=30 June 2016}}</ref> The minister in his speech said that the [[Government of India|Government]] is in favour of exporting the torpedo to friendly nations including [[Vietnam]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/India-joins-elite-group-of-eight-with-anti-submarine-Varunastra-in-arsenal/2016/06/30/article3506714.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160701140833/http://www.newindianexpress.com/nation/India-joins-elite-group-of-eight-with-anti-submarine-Varunastra-in-arsenal/2016/06/30/article3506714.ece |url-status=dead |archive-date=1 July 2016 |title=India joins elite group of eight with anti-submarine Varunastra in arsenal |work=The New Indian Express |date=30 June 2016}}</ref><ref name="varunastraExport" /> With some minor modifications the submarine variant of the torpedo is to be test fired shortly.<ref name="varunastraIndiaToday">{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/indian-navy-inducts-indigenous-heavyweight-torpedo-varunastra-17050-2016-06-29|title=Indian Navy inducts indigenous heavyweight torpedo Varunastra|work=India Today|agency=IANS|date=29 June 2016|access-date=30 June 2016}}</ref>

During [[Aero India|Aero India 2017]], it was reported that DRDO has begun test-firing of a submarine-launched variant of the torpedo. A [[Sindhughosh-class submarine]] is being used as the launch platform for the development. The variant was reportedly accepted and ready for production.<ref name="it-15feb172">{{cite news |last1=Purohit |first1=Jugal R |date=15 February 2017 |title=India to fire self-made torpedo VARUNASTRA from our submarines, says DRDO |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/varunastra-drdo-defence-research-and-development-organisation-torpedo-submarines-mtcr-lca-tejas-960903-2017-02-15 |work=India Today |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=India To Test Fire Home-Made Torpedo From Russian EKM Class Submarine |url=http://www.defenseworld.net/news/18497/India_To_Test_Fire_Home_Made_Torpedo_From_Russian_EKM_Class_Submarine |access-date=20 February 2017 |website=www.defenseworld.net |archive-date=20 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220185717/http://www.defenseworld.net/news/18497/India_To_Test_Fire_Home_Made_Torpedo_From_Russian_EKM_Class_Submarine |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 5 June 2023, Varunastra was fired by a [[Kamorta-class corvette|''Kamorta''-class corvette]] at an Under Water Target System (UWTS) laid by [[INS Jalashwa|INS ''Jalashwa'']]. This was the first trial where the torpedo was equipped with High Explosive (HE) live warhead.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-06 |title=Indian Navy undertakes first combat firing of Varunastra torpedo |url=https://www.janes.com/osint-insights/defence-news/defence/indian-navy-undertakes-first-combat-firing-of-varunastra-torpedo |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=Default |language=en}}</ref> On 6 June, the Navy successfully conducted a combat trial of Varunastra where the torpedo was fired from a submarine and successfully hit an underwater target.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=MINISTRY OF DEFENCE - YEAR END REVIEW 2023 |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1989502 |access-date=2023-12-27 |website=pib.gov.in}}</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Peri |first=Dinakar |date=2023-06-06 |title=Indigenous heavy weight torpedo hits bull's eye in live test by Indian Navy |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/indigenous-heavy-weight-torpedo-hits-bulls-eye-in-live-test-by-indian-navy/article66939145.ece |access-date=2025-01-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

In September 2024, Apollo Micro Systems Limited received an order for [[Software-defined radio|Software Defined]] Universal Homing System for the Heavy Weight Torpedo from [[Bharat Dynamics Limited]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Apollo Micro Systems wins order from Bharat Dynamics - Check details, Companies News, Business News {{!}} Zee Business |url=https://www.zeebiz.com/companies/news-apollo-micro-systems-order-bharat-dynamics-details-311310/amp |access-date=2024-10-15 |website=www.zeebiz.com}}</ref>

=== Production ===

* '''30 June 2016''': Reports suggested that Varunastra would be manufactured by Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) in association with the [[Naval Science and Technological Laboratory]] (NSTL).<ref name="varunastraFinancialExp" />
* '''4 July 2016''': Order for the first batch of 73 torpedoes at a cost of {{INRConvert|8760|c|year=2016|lk=on}} was placed. The technology was formally handed over to BDL for production. The torpedo will have an indigenous content of 95%. The torpedo was also inducted by the Navy.<ref name="varunastraIndianExp" /><ref name=":2">{{cite news |last1=Bedi |first1=Rahul |date=4 July 2016 |title=Indian Navy inducts indigenous Varunastra heavyweight torpedo |url=http://www.janes.com/article/61975/indian-navy-inducts-indigenous-varunastra-heavyweight-torpedo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202030244/http://www.janes.com/article/61975/indian-navy-inducts-indigenous-varunastra-heavyweight-torpedo |archive-date=2 February 2017 |work=IHS Jane's Defence Weekly}}</ref> All future anti-submarine warfare ships will be capable of firing Varunastra.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Hon'ble RM hands over Varunastra to Indian Navy |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/government-press-release/rm-hands-over-varunastra-torpedo-to-indian-navy-116062901353_1.html |access-date=30 June 2016 |website=Business Standard}}</ref><ref name="varunastraUPI">{{cite web |last=Ziezulewicz |first=Geoff |date=30 June 2016 |title=Varunastra missile handed over to Indian navy |url=http://www.upi.com/Business_News/Security-Industry/2016/06/30/Varunastra-missile-handed-over-to-Indian-navy/7501467295879/ |work=UPI}}</ref>
* '''11 April 2018''': BDL signed a Licensing Agreement for Transfer of Technology with NSTL for the production, testing and maintenance of Varunastra torpedoes.<ref>{{cite news|title=BDL to make 'Varunastra'|url=http://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-telangana/bdl-to-make-varunastra/article23507735.ece|work=The Hindu|date=12 April 2018|language=en-IN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=BDL Inks ToT Agreement with NSTL |url=https://www.psuconnect.in/memorandum-of-understanding/bdl-inks-tot-agreement-with-nstl-for-product-ionization-of-varunastra |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=www.psuconnect.in |language=en}}</ref>
* '''14 June 2019''': [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]] awarded a contract worth {{INRConvert|1187|c|year=2019}} to BDL to supply 63 Varunastra torpedoes to the Indian Navy.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rao |first1=Sushil |title=India set to join heavyweight torpedo club |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/india-set-to-join-heavyweight-torpedo-club/articleshow/69780343.cms |work=The Times of India |date=14 June 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2020-01-09 |title=Indian Navy to soon get first batch of indigenously-built torpedo Varunastra |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report-indian-navy-to-soon-get-first-batch-of-indigenously-built-torpedo-varunastra-2808706 |access-date=2020-01-15 |website=[[DNA India]] |language=en}}</ref>
* '''February 2020''': Reports suggested that first batch of torpedoes from second order would be delivered soon.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Aryasamaj |first=Team |date=2020-02-03 |title=Indigenous 'Varunastra' To Be Fitted in Indian Submarines And Ships |url=https://aryasamajkerala.org.in/indigenous-varunastra-to-be-fitted-in-indian-submarines-and-ships/ |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=Arya Samajam Kerala - Official {{!}} आ नो भद्राः क्रतवो यन्तु विश्वतः |language=en-US}}</ref>
* '''20 March 2025''': Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) cleared the Acceptance of Necessity for an additional batch of ship-launched variant of Varunastra Torpedo (Combat).<ref>{{Cite news |date=20 March 2025 |title=DAC clears capital acquisition proposals worth over Rs 54,000 crore to enhance defence capabilities |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2113268 |access-date=20 March 2025 |work=[[Press Information Bureau]]}}</ref>

== Further development ==

=== Thermal Heavy Weight Torpedo Shakti ===
[[File:Shakti Thermal Torpedo.jpg|thumb|Shakti Thermal Torpedo]]
Shakti heavyweight torpedo uses thermal propulsion technology in contrast to the Varunastra torpedo which uses electric propulsion. The torpedo employs [[monopropellant]] fuel, which allows combustion to take place without aerial oxygen, and a [[Pump-jet|pumpjet]]. Its propulsion unit generates 400 kW of power for faster acceleration. A newer propulsion unit is under development which will be producing 500 kW of power .It can operate at a maximum depth of {{convert|600|m|ft}}, a maximum speed of {{convert|60|kn}}. The first image emerged publicly in [[Twitter]] on 9 June 2023 which hinted that the torpedo is undergoing sea trials.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chauhan, AVSM & Bar, VSM |first=Retd Vice Admiral Pradeep |date=2017-02-09 |title=India's Submarine Arm — Returning to Even-Trim |url=https://cimsec.org/indias-submarine-arm-returning-even-trim/ |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Center for International Maritime Security |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-29 |title=Indian Navy test fires Shakti thermal torpedo |url=https://indiandefenseanalysis.com/2023/06/29/indian-navy-test-fires-shakti-thermal-torpedo/ |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=Indian Defense Analysis |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sri |first=Aman |date=2023-07-22 |title=India getting a new secret torpedo? |url=https://www.brahmastra.ltd/post/india-getting-a-new-secret-torpedo |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=brahmastraspace |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1667036821426151424 |user=PRO_Vizag |title=Alarm Torpedo – Enemy Beware!! |date=2023-06-09 |access-date=2024-08-30}}</ref>

=== Electronic Heavy Weight Torpedo Takshak ===
Takshak torpedo is the advanced version of the Varunastra torpedo which employs an electric battery for propulsion. It has a length of {{convert|6.4|m|ft}} which is shorter from the previous variant, enabling to be launched from submarines. The torpedo had a range of {{Convert|40|km|abbr=on}} and maximum depth of {{Convert|400|m|ft|abbr=on}}. Takshak uses a “swim-out” launch system, which launches torpedoes without compressed air and minimises [[acoustic signature]] during launch. It also features [[Ring laser gyroscope|ring laser gyro]] [[inertial navigation system]] (RLG INS) as well as [[Global Positioning System|GPS]]/[[Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System|NavIC]]-based guidance. Takshak has 2 variants: submarine-launched with optical fiber guidance and ship-launched with autonomous guidance. By May 2024, the torpedo was ready for sea trials with the Indian Navy which would pave way for its induction and deployment.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Subramanian |first=T. S. |title=Underwater might |url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/other/article30164828.ece |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928105811/https://frontline.thehindu.com/other/article30164828.ece |archive-date=2021-09-28 |access-date=2020-09-20 |website=Frontline |language=en|date=2012-03-23}}</ref><ref name=":5" />

On 30 December 2024, the Indian [[Ministry of Defence (India)|Ministry of Defence]] (MoD) signed a contract, worth {{INRConvert|877|c|lk=on|year=2024|}}, with the French [[Naval Group]] to integrate DRDO developed Electronic Heavy Weight Torpedo Takshak (EHWT) on [[Kalvari-class submarine (2015)|Kalvari-class submarines]].<ref>{{cite news |date=30 December 2024 |title=Rs 877 crore contract signed with Naval Group, France for integration of Electronic Heavy Weight Torpedo to augment fire power capabilities of Kalvari-Class submarines |url=https://pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2088874 |access-date=31 December 2024 |publisher=Press Information Bureau |agency=Ministry of Defence, Government of India}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-11-22 |title=First production Varunastra Heavy Weight Torpedo sent to the Indian Navy |url=https://frontierindia.com/first-production-varunastra-heavy-weight-torpedo-sent-to-the-indian-navy/?srsltid=AfmBOooGKEc-hubQDNH96I9G_DXAnhd5khYc0HwuBAsXEi6FcrottEKK |access-date=2024-12-30 |website=Frontier India |language=en}}</ref> The guidance software of the torpedo will be integrated with the Submarine Tactical Integrated Combat System (SUBTICS) of the Kalvari submarines.<ref name=":5" />

The torpedo trials from the class of submarines is expected before the end of 2026, as of April 2026. The trial campaign will begin with dry and wet trials in harbour to ensure that the torpedo can be launched without damage to the submarine's sensors and external surface. If successful, it will be followed by trials using live warheads by 2027 on decommissioned ships or underwater targets.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=2026-04-06 |title=Big lift for Indian Navy submarines as 'Takshak' electric heavyweight torpedoes to begin trials soon: Report |url=https://www.theweek.in/news/defence/2026/04/06/big-lift-for-indian-navy-submarines-as-takshak-electric-heavyweight-torpedoes-to-begin-trials-soon-report.html |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=The Week |language=en}}</ref>

A Wire Guided Heavy Weight Torpedo (WGHWT) is also under development with the DRDO as of 2026. It is a submarine launched torpedo with high speeds. WGHWT and EHWT could be different designations for the same design.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Menon |first=Adithya Krishna |date=2026-01-29 |title=India showcases first Hypersonic Anti-Ship Missile System in national parade |url=https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/01/india-showcases-first-hypersonic-anti-ship-missile-system-in-national-parade/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129170623/https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/01/india-showcases-first-hypersonic-anti-ship-missile-system-in-national-parade/ |archive-date=2026-01-29 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Naval News |language=en-US}}</ref> The first production grade was delivered by BDL from its Hyderabad facility to NSTL's Visakhapatnam unit on 25 April 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Today |first=Telangana |date=2026-04-25 |title=BDL delivers India's first indigenous Wire Guided Heavy Weight Torpedo |url=https://telanganatoday.com/bdl-delivers-indias-first-indigenous-wire-guided-heavy-weight-torpedo |access-date=2026-04-25 |website=Telangana Today |language=en}}</ref>

extract: The Varunastra (lit. 'Astra (weapon) of Varuna') is an Indian advanced autonomous heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo, developed by the Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL) of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) for the Indian Navy. It is named after a legendary weapon created by the Hindu god of the oceans, Varuna.
